items.title: Welcome by the School Board President

publicComments.name: Douglas Alsop
publicComments.summary: His written concern about four portables being permanent was addressed by Trustee McBride, who confirmed DSA rules limit portables to two years; Alsop was satisfied with that answer and did not speak in person.

publicComments.name: Maureen McPeek
publicComments.summary: A Roosevelt second-grade teacher urged the board to wait until January 2021 to reopen, citing inadequate safety preparations, temperature-checking issues, lack of PPE, and concerns that behavior management would crowd out academic instruction.

publicComments.name: Jackie Moore
publicComments.summary: A Hoover special day class teacher argued for continuing full distance learning, citing COVID prevention, positive distance-learning outcomes for her SDC students, and personal financial inability to take unpaid leave.

publicComments.name: Nusheen Kavyani
publicComments.summary: A parent stated that current reopening plans carry the risks of COVID without the benefits of in-person learning, and urged that chat be open for public viewing to better simulate a public meeting.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiatkowski
publicComments.summary: A child psychiatrist described alarming mental health trends among students during distance learning and proposed a pilot program using willing teachers and families as a first step toward cautious reopening.

publicComments.name: Sarah Henderson Martinez
publicComments.summary: A preschool teacher expressed concern about inadequate contact tracing, risk to elderly family members, children's inability to wear masks, a classroom move mid-year, and urged caution before reopening.

publicComments.name: Kathryn Stewart
publicComments.summary: A parent argued that teachers' lives are valuable enough for parents to tolerate the inconvenience of distance learning until it is truly safe for teachers to return, and pushed back on prioritizing children's social-emotional comfort over teacher safety.

publicComments.name: Eric Sutton
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent reported that 65% of first-grade Orion families preferred distance learning and 100% wanted to keep their current teachers, warned that the district's proposal would destroy the school's effective two-teacher distance model, and disputed blaming mental illness on distance learning.

publicComments.name: Christy Herrera
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten teacher argued the district should not reopen until the county reaches the yellow tier, said five-year-olds cannot developmentally comply with masking and distancing requirements, and described severe stress and health impacts on teachers caused by reopening pressure.

publicComments.name: Indra Hernandez
publicComments.summary: A preschool teacher said distance learning is working, urged the board to ensure preschool receives the same safety protocols as the rest of the district, and asked that safety come first so staff can continue to serve children.

publicComments.name: Ramin Kaivan
publicComments.summary: A business owner and husband of a preschool teacher argued that distance learning is working in his home, disputed mental health statistics, and warned that returning young children who cannot comply with PPE requirements would be dangerous.

publicComments.name: Laura Atherton
publicComments.summary: A special day class preschool teacher explained that her students cannot wear masks, require diaper changes and hand-over-hand feeding, and that physical distancing is impossible with young children with special needs, urging the board not to reopen preschool SDC.

publicComments.name: Mohammad Tabrizi
publicComments.summary: A parent urged the board to compare RCSD's reopening plan with Menlo Park City School District's more thorough plan, argued the district was ill-prepared to reopen safely, and called for rigorous safety and testing protocols as a prerequisite.

publicComments.name: Christina Kim
publicComments.summary: An Orion Mandarin Immersion parent reported that their community's own survey showed high flexibility and a strong desire to keep the MI program intact, and requested that the board support site-specific, collaborative solutions.

publicComments.name: Christina Hsu
publicComments.summary: An Orion Mandarin Immersion parent said the district survey caused confusion and anxiety in their community, and asked the board to allow individual sites and programs to work with their teachers and administrators on models that fit their specific needs.

publicComments.name: Devin/Michelle Mulaney
publicComments.summary: Speaker yielded their time without making substantive comments.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: A parent called for respectful, fact-based dialogue, asked teachers to articulate what they need to return safely, urged the board to speak up for the most vulnerable students, and noted that learning pods in his experience are working safely.

publicComments.name: Linda Elkins
publicComments.summary: A parent of three district students gave feedback that the survey's forced-choice format obscured nuances around teacher continuity, expressed support for a return to in-person learning in some form, and suggested leveraging parent expertise in planning.

publicComments.name: Melanie Haskell
publicComments.summary: A first-grade parent asked the board to continue offering independent study as an option regardless of the in-person decision, and recommended involving parents meaningfully in reopening committees as Menlo Park had done.

publicComments.name: Kerry Schmidt
publicComments.summary: A bilingual kindergarten teacher with 25 years in the district said she would love to be back in person but that returning without proper safety measures would not provide a safe learning environment and would distract from teaching.

publicComments.name: Kamli Nannini
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten parent and physician with an epidemiology background argued that teachers are essential workers, that actual COVID transmission risk from masked asymptomatic children is likely negligible, and that hearing from medical experts would increase teacher willingness to return.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: An Orion parent and PTO leader expressed frustration that the Orion program feels perpetually at risk, asked the board to stop characterizing Orion families as well-resourced, and urged genuine partnership and investment in program stability.

publicComments.name: Michelle Smith
publicComments.summary: An Adelante Selby parent expressed concern about the Spanish immersion program being at risk, noted that masks prevent teachers from modeling mouth movements for language learning, and raised worries about building ventilation and air quality.

publicComments.name: Michelle Butler
publicComments.summary: A teacher who uses a wheelchair said she loves her students and wants to return when safe, explained she is pursuing the interactive process but fears losing her job, and said managing COVID safety compliance would prevent effective reading instruction.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Serrano
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten teacher with 37 years of experience warned that class reconfiguration would restart the exhausting relationship-building process, said site-specific concerns should drive reopening decisions, and noted she cannot ensure families of her Latinx students are following the four pillars.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: A speaker suggested bringing back older students (grades 2–5) first rather than the youngest, since they can better manage masks and distancing, and asked the board to wait at least until the end of the first trimester before reopening any grade.

publicComments.name: Keely Vega
publicComments.summary: A kindergarten parent asked the board to respond to the suggestion of launching a willing-cohort pilot program and to explain how the district is learning from schools like Menlo Park that have already reopened.
